newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA ON VERGE OF TEST WIN AGAINST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA ON VERGE OF TEST WIN AGAINST INDIA.

text.p: Superb fast bowling from their four-man pace battery left South Africa on the verge of victory at tea in the first test against India on Saturday.

South Africa's spearhead Allan Donald rocked the Indian top order with an opening spell of 3-10 in six overs and, by the interval, India were precariously placed on 55 for eight in their second innings.
Shaun Pollock and Lance Klusener , took two wickets apiece on a Kingsmead pitch still offering pace and bounce.

However, Rahul Dravid, batting confidently at number six for an unbeaten 21, at least ensured that India surpassed their lowest-ever test total of 42 all out -- achieved against England at Lord's in 1974.

India had been set an improbable victory target of 395 after South Africa were bowled out for 259 in their second innings shortly before lunch. Brian McMillan finished on 51 not out and seamer Venkatesh Prasad took 5-93 for match figures of 10-153 - his first 10-wicket haul at test level.
A fired-up Donald removed Vikram Rathore and Saurav Ganguly in his first over before lunch.
He then bowled left-handed opener Woorkeri Raman for one with an inswinging full toss three overs after the interval to leave India reeling at seven for three.

The experienced pair of Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin tried to repair some of the damage for the fourth wicket but could add only eight runs before Tendulkar was brilliantly caught by Gary Kirsten in the gully.
With his score on four, Tendulkar drove at a Pollock delivery and the catch stuck in Kirsten's right hand as he acrobatically dived sideways.
Pollock then took the key wicket of Azharuddin when the former Indian captain mistimed an on-drive to Klusener at wide mid-on and India had subsided to 20 for five.
Klusener then removed Nayan Mongia and Anil Kumble to reduce India to 40 for seven before short leg Adam Bacher produced quick reflexes to run out Javagal Srinath for seven in the 27th over.
